source_name: Camunda - the product blog (camunda.com/blog) plus the docs tree the assignment pairs it with (docs.camunda.io, docs.camunda.org)
enumeration_method: Blog half: https://camunda.com/blog/sitemap.xml (fetched 2026-09-26, 461191 bytes) carries 1453 <loc> entries which are 1435 unique URLs, every one of them a post of the form https://camunda.com/blog/YYYY/MM/<slug>/ - the 18-entry delta is exact duplicate <loc> entries, and no <loc> is a tag, author or category index. The frozen frontier is those 1435 posts in sitemap order (ledgers/camunda-docs-blog.frontier.txt). The assignment's population_estimate was 120, which is 12x low for the blog alone; the sitemap count is used, and this divergence is recorded rather than reconciled. Docs half: the docs subtree is NOT enumerable from this machine (see blocked_component) - the four URLs that could be named without guessing are frontier items 1436-1439. population_size is therefore 1435 blog posts + 4 docs entry points = 1439, and the ledger carries one row per frontier item.
facet_cross_check: The three AI facets of the blog were harvested through the client-rendered index (30-40 x 600 ms scrolls plus a DOM harvest of a[href*="/blog/"]) and compared against the frozen frontier: tag/ai -> 9 posts, tag/agentic-ai -> 9 posts, category/agentic-orchestration -> 9 posts, of which 0 were missing from the frontier (missing = [] for all three, saved as ledgers/camunda-docs-blog.raw/tag_ai.json, tag_agentic-ai.json, category_agentic-orchestration.json). The facets were used only as a cross-check: the population was never narrowed by keyword, and the unfiltered enumeration is the sitemap.
browser_tool: chrome-devtools-mcp (shared Chrome instance, my own tab) for the facet indexes and the artefact pages; curl for the population fetch
artefact_routes: Preference order for a process artefact in this source, per the assignment: (a) a .bpmn asset link, which yields decisive BPMN 2.0 XML; (b) a native-resolution of a modelled diagram; (c) docs prose naming the model elements. The screen of every saved post records imgs, files (.bpmn/.dmn/.cmmn), embedded YouTube ids and figure markup, so the route actually used is named in each row's judged_from.
blocked_component: The docs half of the source is unreachable from this machine: docs.camunda.io/sitemap.xml returns curl exit 7 (no connection), docs.camunda.io/ returns 000 in curl and net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED in a fresh Chrome tab, and docs.camunda.org/ behaves the same. The control in the same session returns 200 for https://camunda.com/ and for the blog sitemap. Pinning the hostname to its resolved IP was flagged by the harness as routing around the egress control and was not done, and no proxy, mirror, archive or assistant-side fetch tool was used to reach around it. Because even the sitemap is refused, the size of the docs tree cannot be enumerated and the docs component cannot be a census population; its four nameable entry points are carried as BLOCKED rows (frontier 1436-1439). Full record: sources/OPERATOR-TODO.md P10.
judgment_convention: judgment is true when the verdict required interpretation: every UNCERTAIN, every E1 on a page that does show a drawn diagram, and every E2 on a page that does discuss AI. It is false where the call was mechanical: E0 (no process artefact of any kind), E3, E2 on a page with no AI/LLM keyword anywhere, and E1 on pages whose only images are photographs, logos, product-UI screenshots or code/JSON listings. The mechanical part of each call is re-runnable from ledgers/camunda-docs-blog.raw/screen.jsonl, which holds the extracted text, image list, .bpmn links and AI/LLM term counts for every fetched post.
ai_lexicon: artificial intelligence|artificial intelligence|AI agent|AI Agent|AI-powered|AI powered|GenAI|generative AI|generative AI|LLM|large language model|machine learning|machine-learning|neural|chatbot|copilot|copilot|GPT|OpenAI|Anthropic|Claude|Gemini|prompt|embedding|RAG|retrieval-augmented|agentic|Agentic|agent|Agent|agents|intelligent. Known false positives in this source: Camunda's product names that contain an AI word, and "AI Agent connector" / "AI Agent sub-process", which is AI inside the process and in scope, as against "BPMN Copilot", which generates the diagram and is the E2 case (the assignment calls this distinction out explicitly).
operator_ruling: elicitation-5a, 2026-09-26, relayed from the operator, on recordings: do not open YouTube links and do not play any video; a page that embeds a recording is judged only on what the host page itself shows (poster image, page text). This applies to the blog posts that embed a recording: such a post is judged on its text and its other figures, and an artefact that exists only inside the recording is not an admissible item.
note: Records live under corpus/camunda-docs-blog/ as NNN_<slug>.md beside their NNN_*.png captures. NNN is the record's own sequence, not a frontier index: records were written in the order the per-post rulings were settled, so the frontier index of a post is carried by the `n` field of the record's frontmatter and by the ledger row's `record` path, never by NNN. Every row's evidence field, and every quote in a record, is a verbatim string checked against the text, image alt texts and linked model XML of that post's saved HTML.

title: Revolutionizing Health Insurance Underwriting: Harnessing AI for Smarter, Faster, and Fairer Risk Assessment | Camunda
evidence: prior to underwriter review, you can take advantage of AI to review and summarize various records as well as do an initial risk assessment
question: Are the two magenta tasks 'Gather and Summarize relevant data' and 'Risk Assessment' AI-bound? The page says AI does the pre-underwriting review/summarise and initial risk assessment and these tasks sit exactly there, but neither carries an element-template badge, AI label or prompt binding in the figure (checked at 5x upscale of the full 1293x368 asset).
note: Both of this page's BPMN figures were read natively, because the row's captured figure (1038x524) is only a crop of the process. Full figure (1293x368, fetched from the page's own asset URL and kept at ledgers/camunda-docs-blog.raw/_extra/216_fig1.png): 'Application Submitted' -> 'etermine if Previous or Existing Customer' (sic) -> gateway splitting 'New Customer' ('Update Customer Record'), 'Previous Customer' ('Consider Policy Restatement') and 'Existing Customer' ('Notify Already a Customer' -> end 'Application Interrupted') -> 'Gather and Summarize relevant data' -> 'Risk Assessment' -> 'Notify Customer of Decision' -> XOR 'Continue Application Process?' -> 'Continue' to 'Underwriting Application Review' (user task, amber; boundary error 'Fraud Detected' -> 'Investigate Possible Fraud') -> 'Provide Policy Quote and Documentation' -> end 'Application Accepted', or 'Abort Application Process' -> 'Email with Reasons for Rejection' -> end 'Application Rejected'. The captured 1038x524 crop is the right-hand part of the same diagram, which is why the earlier read saw no AI step. Unresolved: the page states AI does the pre-underwriting work ('...you can take advantage of AI to review and summarize various records as well as do an initial risk assessment'), and the two magenta tasks 'Gather and Summarize relevant data' and 'Risk Assessment' sit exactly at that point of the process - but at 5x upscale (ledgers/camunda-docs-blog.raw/_extra/216_zoom_magenta.png) neither task carries an element-template badge, an AI-naming label, or any prompt/binding, unlike the neighbouring template tasks that do show their icon. So the AI binding is asserted only by the prose and by the tasks' colour, never drawn. Question for the researcher: are those two magenta tasks AI-bound (page prose + colour), or plain tasks coloured for emphasis?
